question.value: Investigate the long-term stability of total flux, fractional polarization, and EVPA, as well as the synchrotron age and frequency-dependent polarization properties of the radio quasar 3C 286 at millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths from 2006 to 2025.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we present the result of polarimetric observations of 3C 286 using ALMA, IRAM, and SMA at 91.5–343.4 GHz, spanning from October 2006 to February 2025.
The combined data from these three monitoring programs allows for a precise investigation of the stability and properties of 3C 286 at millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00001.CAL.

The data has been primarily obtained in Band 3 (91.5 and 103.5 GHz) and Band 7 (343.4 GHz) since May 2018. Data in Band 6 (233.0 GHz) has been obtained less frequently as a complement to the Band 7 data
The observations of 3C 286 were performed with a full polarization mode to obtain all four Stokes parameters.

analysis_steps.goal: Evaluate long-term stability of total flux, EVPA, and fractional polarization and derive reference values

method.value: Divide ALMA data into three time periods (Period I: MJD 58230-59000, Period II: MJD 59200-59900, Period III: after MJD 60100) to compare period averages, fit linear secular trend models to ALMA and IRAM time series (including IRAM Uranus residuals), and compute weighted means across epochs as reference values.

evidence.quote: To investigate this in further detail, we divided the ALMA data into three groups: the first, obtained between MJD 58230 and 59000, referred to as Period I, the second, obtained between MJD 59200 and 59900, referred to as Period II, and the third, after MJD 60100, referred to as Period III.
To further investigate the long-term trend in the ALMA data, we fitted all the total flux measurements at each frequency with the following function: $S_{\nu} = c_0 \times (t-58000) + c_1$
Therefore, we provide the weighted mean of the EVPA and fractional polarization, as well as the total flux, as the reference values for 3C 286 (Table 2).

analysis_steps.goal: Measure spectral indices and spectral break frequency

method.value: Fit power-law spectra (S_nu proportional to nu^-alpha) separately to historical VLA measurements (3-50 GHz) and IRAM reference measurements (86-229 GHz) to determine spectral indices and their intersection (break frequency).

evidence.quote: For the frequencies higher than those covered by VLA, we use only the IRAM measurements to determine the spectral index, as the ALMA flux appears to vary with different rates in different frequency bands.

findings_qualitative.value: The intrinsic total flux of 3C 286 has remained stable up to 229 GHz from 2006 to 2024; the apparent decrease in ALMA flux (2%-15%) is partially attributable (up to 4%) to the brightening of Uranus as its north pole rotates into view while the ESA4 model assumes constant brightness.

evidence.quote: The IRAM measurements from 2006 to 2024 show that the total flux of 3C 286 is stable within measurement uncertainties, indicating long-term stability up to 229 GHz, when applying a fixed Kelvin-to-Jansky conversion factor throughout its dataset.

ALMA data from 2018 to 2024 exhibit a decrease in flux, which up to 4% could be attributed to an apparent increase in the absolute brightness of Uranus, the primary flux calibrator for ALMA with the ESA4 model.

findings_qualitative.value: Both fractional polarization and EVPA of 3C 286 have remained stable over the ~20-year monitoring period across 86 to 343.4 GHz.

evidence.quote: Likewise, long-term monitoring observations with ALMA and IRAM suggest that both EVPA and fractional polarization of 3C 286 have remained nearly constant over the last $\sim$20 years.

findings_qualitative.value: The EVPA rotates and fractional polarization increases with frequency up to 343.4 GHz, both following single power-law relationships with wavelength squared.

evidence.loc: Discussion / EVPA rotation as a function of frequency
evidence.quote: Given that the observed EVPA values are not only well-described by a single power-law function over three orders of magnitude in wavelength squared

Notably, the fractional polarization, spanning four orders of magnitude in wavelength squared, is well-described by a single power-law function with coefficients $k'=-0.047\pm0.001$ and $\rm C'=1.108\pm0.001$ (Figure 10).

findings_qualitative.value: Theoretical EVPA values from the fitted power-law model curve are proposed as a reference for absolute EVPA calibration between 5 and 343.4 GHz.

evidence.quote: We therefore propose using the theoretical EVPA values from this model curve for absolute EVPA calibration between 5 and 343.4 GHz.

claims.hypothesis: The intrinsic total flux density of 3C 286 is stable over time at millimeter wavelengths up to 229 GHz, and the apparent decline in ALMA flux measurements is partially caused by seasonal brightening of the primary flux calibrator Uranus.
claims.experiment: Monitor total flux of 3C 286 with IRAM (86, 229 GHz from 2006 to 2024) using a fixed Kelvin-to-Jansky factor and with ALMA (91.5, 103.5, 233.0, 343.4 GHz from 2018 to 2024) calibrated against the ESA4 Uranus model, and fit linear secular trends to 3C 286 and IRAM Uranus residuals.
claims.result: IRAM fluxes show no clear decreasing trend, while ALMA fluxes decrease by 2%-15% (4% at 91.5 GHz, 2% at 103.5 GHz, 11% at 233.0 GHz, 15% at 343.4 GHz). IRAM 86 GHz residual flux of Uranus increased by 6.6% +/- 1.5% from 2006 to 2024, and ALMA Uranus/Neptune brightness ratio increased by 4%.
claims.finding: The intrinsic total flux of 3C 286 is stable up to 229 GHz; up to 4% of the ALMA flux decrease is explained by Uranus brightening, though the >10% declines in ALMA Bands 6 and 7 require additional instrumental or atmospheric factors.

evidence.quote: The IRAM measurements from 2006 to 2024 show that the total flux of 3C 286 is stable within measurement uncertainties, indicating long-term stability up to 229 GHz, when applying a fixed Kelvin-to-Jansky conversion factor throughout its dataset.
A fit using Equation [eq:fit] to the entire residual flux indicates a systematic increase of 6.6%$\pm$1.5% from 2006 to 2024

Nevertheless, the change in the brightness of Uranus alone cannot fully account for the decreasing trend observed in the ALMA measurements, as the magnitudes of the decrease in Band 6 and 7 exceed 10%.

claims.hypothesis: Thefractional polarization and EVPA of 3C 286 are stable over long timescales at millimeter/submillimeter wavelengths (86-343.4 GHz) and can serve as a high-frequency polarization calibrator reference.
claims.experiment: Analyze multi-year polarimetric time series from ALMA (2018-2024), IRAM (2006-2024), and SMA (2022-2025) by comparing period averages and fitting linear secular trends.
claims.result: Potential secular variations in both EVPA and fractional polarization across all ALMA and IRAM frequencies are smaller than or comparable to measurement uncertainties and standard deviations.
claims.finding: The fractional polarization and EVPA of 3C 286 have remained stable over ~20 years up to 343.4 GHz, allowing high-precision weighted mean reference values to be established.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, the best-fit parameters derived using Equation [eq:fit] indicate that any potential secular changes in both EVPA and fractional polarization during the monitoring period are smaller than or comparable to their standard deviations and/or uncertainties at all frequencies
Likewise, long-term monitoring observations with ALMA and IRAM suggest that both EVPA and fractional polarization of 3C 286 have remained nearly constant over the last $\sim$20 years.

claims.hypothesis: A one-zone continuous injection synchrotron cooling model explains the high-frequency spectral steepening and kinematic age of the 3C 286 jet.
claims.experiment: Measure the spectral break between VLA (3-50 GHz) and IRAM (86-229 GHz) spectra, compute the equipartition magnetic field strength B_eq for a 50 mas source size, and calculate the synchrotron age and apparent expansion speed.
claims.result: The spectrum steepens from alpha = 0.712 +/- 0.003 to 1.039 +/- 0.008 with a break at 67.2 +/- 1.2 GHz. With B_eq ~ 4.4 mG, the synchrotron age is 450 years, implying an apparent speed beta_app = 2.6 for a 50 mas (362 pc) jet.
claims.finding: Because beta_app = 2.6 is much faster than VLBI-measured speeds in 3C 286 (beta_app = 0.6 +/- 0.5) and typical CSS sources (~0.1), a simple one-zone model cannot explain the overall spectrum; a multi-zone interpretation (with a ~3.6 GHz outer-jet break yielding 1950 years and beta_app = 0.6) is required.

evidence.loc: Discussion / Synchrotron age and magnetic field strength
evidence.quote: Substituting the magnetic field strength of 4.4 mG into Equation [eq:tau_syn], we derive the age of 3C 286 to be $\tau_{\rm syn}$=450 years. Given that the source size of 50 mas corresponds to 362 pc, this age implies an average apparent speed $\beta_{\rm app}=2.6$.

evidence.loc: Discussion / Synchrotron age and magnetic field strength
evidence.quote: This, in turn, implies that the overall spectrum may not be fully explained by a one-zone synchrotron model and may instead require a more complex, multi-zone interpretation.

claims.hypothesis: The frequency-dependent EVPA rotation and increasing fractional polarization of 3C 286 from 5 to 343.4 GHz are caused by Faraday rotation and reduced Faraday depolarization in a conical jet with core-shift.
claims.experiment: Fit single power-law functions of wavelength squared to EVPA and fractional polarization from VLA, IRAM, SMA, and ALMA data, derive rest-frame RM between adjacent frequency pairs, and fit |RM| as a power law of frequency.
claims.result: EVPA is well fit by log(chi) = (-0.016 +/- 0.002) log(lambda^2) + (1.547 +/- 0.003); rest-frame |RM| increases from 23 to (3.2 +/- 1.5) x 10^4 rad m^-2 following |RM| proportional to nu^a with a = 2.05 +/- 0.06; fractional polarization follows log(m) = (-0.047 +/- 0.001) log(lambda^2) + (1.108 +/- 0.001).
claims.finding: The RM frequency scaling (a = 2.05 +/- 0.06) matches the theoretical prediction (a = 2) of the Blandford & Konigl conical jet model with core-shift, and the increase in fractional polarization at shorter wavelengths reflects reduced Faraday depolarization.

evidence.loc: Discussion / EVPA rotation as a function of frequency
evidence.quote: The best-fit line represents $\mid$RM~core,$\nu$~$\mid\propto \nu^{a}$ with the power-law index $a=2.05\pm0.06$, which is consistent with the theoretically expected value of $a=2$ for the BK conical jet model.

This closely resembles the EVPA distribution, which is also well fitted with a single power-law, suggesting that at shorter wavelengths, less efficient Faraday depolarization entails the increase of the fractional polarization.

why_this_data.value: Combining long-term multi-frequency monitoring from ALMA, IRAM, and SMA overcomes the low brightness and large uncertainties of 3C 286 at millimeter/submillimeter wavelengths that previously hindered stability and trend analyses. Pre-2022 SMA archival data and 1.4 GHz MeerKAT EVPA data were excluded to avoid systematic calibration offsets and large frequency-dependent uncertainties.

evidence.quote: The combined data from these three monitoring programs allows for a precise investigation of the stability and properties of 3C 286 at millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths.

However, we do not include these measurements in our analysis due to inconsistencies in the flux calibration process and transitions from older solar system models to the CASA-standard models during the monitoring.
We did not include $\chi=29.2^\circ$ at 1.4 GHz obtained with MeerKAT in the RM calculation, due to its frequency-dependent uncertainties of up to 3$^\circ$ (see Figure 2 in (cite: taylor24)).

why_this_method.value: Only IRAM flux measurements were used for the high-frequency spectral index because ALMA fluxes showed band-dependent secular declines; stacking all stable polarization epochs into weighted means and fitting a smooth power-law curve reduces statistical uncertainties in pairwise RM estimates.

evidence.quote: This stability allows us to obtain the fractional polarization and EVPA values with unprecedented accuracy at millimeter/submillimeter wavelengths by stacking all the data.

For the frequencies higher than those covered by VLA, we use only the IRAM measurements to determine the spectral index, as the ALMA flux appears to vary with different rates in different frequency bands.

evidence.loc: Discussion / EVPA rotation as a function of frequency
evidence.quote: Since these model EVPAs along the best-fit curve are derived from a fit to multiple data points, their statistical uncertainties are smaller than those of individual EVPA measurements by a factor of the square root of the number of EVPA measurements.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gradual change in magnetic field direction with optical depth as the cause of EVPA rotation, considered alongside Faraday rotation with core-shift.

evidence.loc: Discussion / EVPA rotation as a function of frequency
evidence.quote: If the direction of the magnetic field gradually changes with optical depth, it could explain the observed EVPA rotation with frequency (cite: agudo12; nagai16).
Alternatively, it can also be explained with Faraday rotation, without requiring magnetic fields that gradually change direction with optical depth.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: One-zone synchrotron cooling model rejected in favor of a multi-zone model (with inner jet break at 67 GHz and outer jet break at ~3.6 GHz) due to implausibly high apparent jet speed (beta_app = 2.6).

evidence.loc: Discussion / Synchrotron age and magnetic field strength
evidence.quote: This, in turn, implies that the overall spectrum may not be fully explained by a one-zone synchrotron model and may instead require a more complex, multi-zone interpretation.

evidence.loc: Discussion / Synchrotron age and magnetic field strength
evidence.quote: Specifically, if the 67 GHz break traces synchrotron aging in the inner jet while the 3.6 GHz break corresponds to the outer jet at 50 mas, the inferred synchrotron age of the outer jet becomes 1950 years.

limitations_admitted.value: 3C 286 is observed at low elevations from ALMA (maximum elevation 37 deg), is weak at high frequencies, and is opposite in RA to Uranus, making its flux calibration dependent on secondary quasar transfer.

evidence.quote: However, 3C 286 is at low elevations for ALMA (with the maximum elevation of 37$^\circ$) and its flux is relatively weak at higher frequencies. In addition, its flux calibration primarily relies on flux transfer from quasars, as its right ascension is opposite to the main planetary primary calibrators.

limitations_admitted.value: The SMA SMAPOL monitoring period (June 2022 to February 2025) is too short to test the long-term total flux stability of 3C 286.

evidence.quote: We do not use the SMA data to test the flux stability of 3C 286, as its monitoring period from June 2022 to February 2025 is too short for a reliable investigation.

limitations_admitted.value: Uranus brightening (up to 4%) cannot fully account for the >10% total flux decreases observed in ALMA Bands 6 and 7.

evidence.quote: Nevertheless, the change in the brightness of Uranus alone cannot fully account for the decreasing trend observed in the ALMA measurements, as the magnitudes of the decrease in Band 6 and 7 exceed 10%.

limitations_admitted.value: IRAM EVPA uncertainties at 229 GHz (average 5.1 deg) appear to be underestimated compared to the standard deviation of the measurements (9.6 deg).

evidence.quote: Moreover, the average of the EVPA uncertainties for IRAM at 229 GHz is 5.1$^\circ$, while the standard deviation of those measurements is 9.6$^\circ$. This discrepancy suggests that the EVPA uncertainties for IRAM may have been underestimated.

limitations_admitted.value: IRAM flux measurements at 86 GHz could be underestimated by ~2% because the conversion factor was derived from 2006-2014 data while the ESA4 model best matches Uranus around 2017.

evidence.quote: Given that the ESA4 model appears to agree best with the data around 2017 (Figure 5), the IRAM flux measurements could have been underestimated by $\sim2\%$ at 86 GHz, although their stability remains intact.

limitations_admitted.value: Standard theoretical depolarization models assume optically thin emission and are not directly applicable to 3C 286 because its emitting regions are partially optically thick and exhibit core-shift.

evidence.quote: However, those models are primarily suited for optically thin cases, whereas the emitting regions in 3C 286 are partially optically thick, exhibiting the core-shift effect.

referee_caveats_inferred: The pairwise rotation measure (RM) values in Table 4 and the power-law fit |RM| proportional to nu^a are not derived from independent frequency pairs, but are sampled from a single smooth power-law fit to EVPA vs lambda^2; therefore, the reported uncertainties and power-law slope a = 2.05 +/- 0.06 are mathematically coupled to the assumed functional form log(chi) = k log(lambda^2) + C.

In Table 4, the rest-frame RM for 103-233 GHz is printed as (8.6 +/- 1.7) x 10^4 rad m^-2, which is a factor of 10 higher than (1+z)^2 times the observing-frame RM of (2.5 +/- 0.4) x 10^3 rad m^-2 (~8.5 x 10^3 rad m^-2), indicating a likely typographical error in the exponent.

Single-dish and connected-element interferometers (VLA, IRAM 30-m, SMA, ALMA 7-m) integrate emission over the entire CSS source (core plus steep-spectrum jet components C1, C2, and outer lobes), so attributing the integrated EVPA rotation and depolarization purely to core-shift in an optically thick conical core ignores frequency-dependent spectral blending between the core and steeper-spectrum jet knots.
